detailed_findings.finding: The argument correctly proves g(n) >= n using that g(1),...,g(n) are n distinct positive integers in increasing order.
The telescoping step and termwise lower bound are valid: summing from k = n to g(n)-1 gives exactly g(n)-n terms, and monotonicity implies g(g(k)) >= g(g(n)) on this range.
detailed_findings.location: proof of the first displayed inequality

detailed_findings.finding: The derivation of the equivalent inequality by dividing through by the positive real (g(g(n)))^r is valid.

reason: The proof is correct and complete. It first establishes g(n) >= n from strict monotonicity and positivity, then telescopes g(g(n)) - g(n) over k = n,...,g(n)-1 and applies the hypothesis termwise. Monotonicity gives g(g(k)) >= g(g(n)) for all such k, so each summand is at least (g(g(n)))^r, yielding the factor g(n)-n. The final rearrangement/division by the positive quantity (g(g(n)))^r validly gives g(g(n))^(1-r) >= g(n)-n. This matches the lemma sketch and role in the assembly.
